verses.text: “Keep silent before me, una islands! Make di peoples renew dem strength. Make dem come near. Den make dem speak. Make we come near together for judgment.
Who don raise up one from di east? Who don call am to im foot in righteousness? E give nations to am, and make am rule over kings. E give dem as dust to im sword, as driven stubble to im bow.
E pursue dem, and pass safely, even by way wey im feet never waka before.
Who don work and do am, calling di generations from di beginning? I, di Lord, di first, and with di last, I be am.”
Di islands don see, and fear. Di ends of di earth tremble. Dem draw near and come.
Everyone help im neighbour, and talk to im brother, “Dey strong.”
So di craftsman encourage di goldsmith, and e wey smooth with hammer encourage am wey strike di anvil, say of di soldering, “E good.” E fasten am with nails, so that e no go move.
“But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob wey I don choose, di offspring of Abraham my friend,
you wey I don take from di ends of di earth, and call from di farthest corners of am, and talk to you, ‘You na my servant, I don choose you and no cast you away.’
No fear, because I dey with you. No dey dismayed, because I be your God. I go strengthen you. Yes, I go help you. Yes, I go uphold you with di right hand of my righteousness.
See, all dem wey dey angry against you go dey ashamed and confounded. Dem wey strive with you go be as nothing, and go perish.
You go seek dem, and no go find dem, even dem wey contend with you. Dem wey war against you go be as nothing, as non-existent thing.
Because I, di Lord your God, go hold your right hand, and talk to you, ‘No fear. I go help you.’
No fear, you worm Jacob, and you men of Israel. I go help you,” talk di Lord, “and your Redeemer na di Holy One of Israel.
See, I don make you new sharp threshing sledge wey get teeth. You go thresh di mountains, and beat dem small, and go make di hills like chaff.
You go winnow dem, and di wind go carry dem away, and di whirlwind go scatter dem. You go rejoice for di Lord. You go glory for di Holy One of Israel.
Di poor and needy dey seek water, and e no dey. Dem tongue fail for thirst. I, di Lord, go answer dem. I, di God of Israel, no go forsake dem.
I go open rivers on di bare heights, and fountains for di middle of di valleys. I go make di wilderness pool of water, and di dry land springs of water.
I go plant for di wilderness di cedar, di acacia, di myrtle and di olive tree. I go set for di desert di cypress, di plane tree and di pine together,
so that dem go see, and know, and consider, and understand together, say di hand of di Lord don do dis, and di Holy One of Israel don create am.”
“Present your case,” talk di Lord. “Bring your strong reasons,” talk di King of Jacob.
“Make dem bring dem forth, and declare to us wetin go happen. Declare di former things, wetin dem be, so that we go consider dem, and know di end of dem; or make us hear di things wey dey come.
Declare di things wey go come afterward, so that we go know say una be gods. Yes, do good, or do evil, so that we go dey dismayed and see am together.
See, una na nothing, and una work na nothing. Anyone wey choose una na abomination.
I don raise up one from di north, and e don come, from di rising of di sun, one wey go call on my name. E go come on rulers as on mortar, and as potter tread clay.
Who don declare am from di beginning, so that we go know? Or beforetime, so that we go talk, ‘E dey right’? Yes, nobody declare, yes, nobody show, yes, nobody hear una words.
I be di first to talk to Zion, ‘See, see dem.’ I give to Jerusalem one wey bring good news.
When I look, no man dey. Among dem no counselor dey, wey, when I ask dem, fit answer word.
See, dem all, dem works na vanity and nothing. Dem molten images na wind and confusion.”
“Look, my servant, wey I uphold; my chosen one, in whom my soul delight. I don put my Spirit on am. E go bring justice to di nations.
E no go cry, nor lift up, nor cause im voice to dey heard for di street.
E no go break bruised reed, and e no go quench dim wick. E go faithfully bring justice.
E no go fail or dey discouraged, until e don set justice for di earth, and di islands go wait for im law.”
Di Lord God, wey create di heavens and stretch dem out, wey spread out di earth and wetin come out of am, wey give breath to di people on am, and spirit to dem wey waka inside am, talk like dis:
“I, di Lord, don call you in righteousness, and I go hold your hand, and I go keep you, and give you for covenant to di people, for light to di nations;
to open di blind eyes, to bring out di prisoners from di dungeon, and dem wey sit for darkness out of di prison.
I be di Lord. Dat na my name. I no go give my glory to another, neither my praise to engraved images.
See, di former things don come to pass, and I declare new things. Before dem spring forth, I tell una about dem.”
Sing to di Lord one new song, im praise from di end of di earth, una wey go down to di sea, and all wey dey inside am, di islands, and di inhabitants of dem.
Make di wilderness and im cities lift up dem voice, di villages wey Kedar dey inhabit. Make di inhabitants of Sela sing. Make dem shout from di top of di mountains.
Make dem give glory to di Lord, and declare im praise for di islands.
Di Lord go go out like mighty man. E go stir up zeal like man of war. E go cry out, yes, e go shout aloud. E go prevail against im enemies.
“I don keep quiet for long time. I don dey still, and restrain myself. Now I go cry out like woman for labour. I go gasp and pant together.
I go lay waste mountains and hills, and dry up all dem herbs. I go make di rivers islands, and I go dry up di pools.

I go bring di blind by way wey dem no know. I go lead dem for paths wey dem no know. I go make darkness light before dem, and crooked places straight. Dis na di things wey I go do, and I no go forsake dem.
Dem go dey turned back. Dem go dey utterly ashamed, wey trust for engraved images, wey talk to molten images, ‘Una na our gods.’
Hear, una deaf! Look, una blind, so that una go see!
Who dey blind but my servant? Or deaf like my messenger wey I send? Who dey blind like im wey dey at peace with me? Who dey blind like di servant of di Lord?
You see many things, but no observe. Im ears dey open, but e no hear.”
Di Lord dey pleased, for im righteousness sake, to magnify di law and make am honourable.

But dis na people wey dem rob and plunder. Dem all dey trapped for holes, and dey hidden for prisons. Dem don become prey, and nobody dey rescue. Dem don become plunder, and nobody talk, “Restore am!”
Who among una go give ear to dis? Who go listen and hear for di time wey dey come?
Who give Jacob for plunder, and Israel to di robbers? No be di Lord, im against whom we don sin, and for whose ways dem no dey willing to waka, neither dem obey im law?
So e don pour on am di heat of im anger, and di strength of battle. E set am on fire all round, yet e no know. E burn am, yet e no lay am to heart.
But now di Lord wey create you, Jacob, and wey form you, Israel, talk like dis: “No fear, because I don redeem you. I don call you by your name. You be mine.
When you pass through di waters, I go dey with you, and through di rivers, dem no go overwhelm you. When you waka through di fire, you no go dey burned, neither di flame go scorch you.
Because I be di Lord your God, di Holy One of Israel, your Saviour. I don give Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba for you.
Since you dey precious for my eyes, and honoured, and I love you, therefore I go give men for you, and peoples for your life.
No fear, because I dey with you. I go bring your offspring from di east, and gather you from di west.
I go talk to di north, ‘Give up!’ and to di south, ‘No hold back! Bring my sons from far, and my daughters from di end of di earth,
everyone wey dem call by my name, and wey I don create for my glory, wey I don form, yes, wey I don make.’”
Bring out di blind people wey get eyes, and di deaf wey get ears.

Make all di nations dey gathered together, and make di peoples dey assembled. Who among dem fit declare dis, and show us di former things? Make dem bring dem witnesses, so that dem go dey justified, or make dem hear, and talk, “Na true.”
“Una na my witnesses,” talk di Lord, “and my servant wey I don choose, so that una go know and believe me, and understand say I be am. Before me no god dey formed, neither go dey after me.
I, even I, na di Lord, and beside me no saviour dey.
I don declare, and I don save, and I don show, and no strange god dey among una. Therefore una na my witnesses,” talk di Lord, “and I be God.
Yes, since di day dey, I be am. Nobody fit deliver from my hand. I go work, and who go reverse am?”
Di Lord, your Redeemer, di Holy One of Israel, talk like dis: “For your sake I don send to Babylon, and I go bring down all dem as fugitives, even di Chaldeans, for di ships of dem rejoicing.
I be di Lord, your Holy One, di Creator of Israel, your King.”
Di Lord talk like dis, wey make way for di sea, and path for di mighty waters,
wey bring out di chariot and horse, di army and di mighty man (dem lie down together, dem no go rise; dem don extinguish, dem quench like wick):
“No remember di former things, neither consider di things of old.
See, I dey do new thing. Now e go spring forth. Una no go perceive am? I go even make way for di wilderness, and rivers for di desert.
Di animals of di field go honour me, di jackals and di ostriches, because I give water for di wilderness, and rivers for di desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
di people wey I don form for myself, so that dem go declare my praise.
Yet you no call on me, Jacob. But you don dey weary of me, Israel.
You no bring me di sheep of your burnt offerings, neither you honour me with your sacrifices. I no make you serve with offerings, neither I weary you with frankincense.
You no buy me sweet cane with money, neither you fill me with di fat of your sacrifices. But you don make me serve with your sins. You don weary me with your iniquities.
I, even I, na im wey blot out your transgressions for my own sake, and I no go remember your sins.
Put me in remembrance. Make we plead together. Declare your case, so that you go dey justified.
Your first father sin, and your teachers don transgress against me.
Therefore I go profane di princes of di sanctuary, and I go make Jacob dey cursed, and Israel dey insulted.”
“Yet hear now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, wey I don choose.
Di Lord wey make you, and form you from di womb, wey go help you, talk like dis: No fear, Jacob my servant, and you Jeshurun, wey I don choose.
Because I go pour water on im wey dey thirsty, and streams on di dry ground. I go pour my Spirit on your offspring, and my blessing on your descendants.
Dem go spring up among di grass, like willows by di watercourses.
One go talk, ‘I be di Lord own.’ Another go call imself by di name of Jacob. Another go write on im hand, ‘Di Lord own,’ and take di name of Israel.”
Di Lord, di King of Israel, and im Redeemer, di Lord of Armies, talk like dis: “I be di first, and I be di last. Beside me no God dey.
Who be like me? Make am call, and declare am, and set am in order for me, since I appoint di ancient people. Make dem declare di things wey dey come, and wey go happen.
No fear, neither dey afraid. I no tell you from of old, and declare am? Una na my witnesses. Dey God beside me? Yes, no Rock dey. I no know any.”
Dem wey make idols na all vanity, and di things wey dem delight for no go profit. Dem witnesses no see, no know, so dem go dey ashamed.
Who don form god, or cast idol wey no profit anything?
See, all im companions go dey ashamed, and di craftsmen na only men. Make dem all gather together. Make dem stand up. Dem go fear. Dem go dey ashamed together.
Di blacksmith take tool, work di metal over di coals, shape am with hammers, and work am with im strong arm. Yes, e dey hungry, and im strength fail. E no drink water, and e dey faint.
Di carpenter stretch out im line. E mark am with pencil. E shape am with planes, and mark am with compass, and e make am after di figure of man, according to di beauty of man, to dwell for house.
E cut down cedars for imself, and take cypress and oak, and strengthen for imself among di trees of di forest. E plant fir tree, and di rain nourish am.
Den e go be for man to burn. E take some of am and warm imself. Yes, e kindle am and bake bread. Yes, e make god and worship am. E make am idol, and fall down before am.
E burn part of am for fire. Over dis part e eat meat. E roast meat and dey satisfied. Yes, e warm imself, and talk, “Aha, I dey warm. I don see fire.”
Di rest of am e make into god, im idol. E fall down to am and worship, and pray to am, and talk, “Deliver me, because you be my god.”
Dem no know, neither dem understand, because e don shut dem eyes, so dem no fit see, and dem hearts, so dem no fit understand.

No one consider, neither dey knowledge nor understanding to talk, “I don burn part of am for fire. Yes, I don also bake bread on im coals. I don roast meat and eat am. I go make di rest of am abomination? I go fall down to block of wood?”
E feed on ashes. Deceived heart don turn am aside, and e no fit deliver im soul, nor talk, “Lie no dey for my right hand?”
Remember dis, Jacob, and Israel, because you be my servant. I don form you. You be my servant. Israel, I no go forget you.
I don blot out, like thick cloud, your transgressions, and like cloud, your sins. Return to me, because I don redeem you.

Sing, una heavens, because di Lord don do am! Shout, una lower parts of di earth! Break out into singing, una mountains, di forest, and every tree inside am, because di Lord don redeem Jacob, and e go glorify imself for Israel.
Di Lord, your Redeemer, and wey form you from di womb, talk like dis: “I be di Lord, wey make all things, wey stretch out di heavens alone, wey spread out di earth by myself,
wey frustrate di signs of di liars, and make diviners mad, wey turn wise men backward, and make dem knowledge foolishness,

wey confirm di word of im servant, and perform di counsel of im messengers, wey talk of Jerusalem, ‘E go dey inhabited,’ and of di cities of Judah, ‘Dem go dey built,’ and I go raise up di ruins of dem;
wey talk to di deep, ‘Dry up, and I go dry up your rivers’;
wey talk of Cyrus, ‘E na my shepherd, and e go perform all my pleasure,’ even saying of Jerusalem, ‘E go dey built,’ and of di temple, ‘Your foundation go dey laid.’”
Di Lord talk like dis to im anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I don hold, to subdue nations before am, and strip kings of dem armour, to open doors before am, so that gates no go dey shut:
“I go go before you, and make di rough places smooth. I go break in pieces di doors of brass, and cut apart di bars of iron.
I go give you di treasures of darkness, and hidden riches of secret places, so that you go know say I, di Lord, wey call you by your name, na di God of Israel.
For Jacob my servant sake, and Israel my chosen, I don call you by your name. I don surname you, though you no know me.
I be di Lord, and dey no other. Beside me dey no God. I go strengthen you, though you no know me,
so that dem go know from di rising of di sun, and from di west, say dey none beside me. I be di Lord, and dey no other.
I form light and create darkness. I make peace and create calamity. I, di Lord, do all dis things.

Drop down, una heavens, from above, and make di skies pour down righteousness. Make di earth open, make salvation bring forth, and make am cause righteousness to spring up with am. I, di Lord, don create am.
Woe to am wey strive with im Maker, clay pot among clay pots! Di clay go talk to am wey form am, ‘Wetin you dey make?’ or ‘Your work no get handles’?
Woe to am wey talk to im father, ‘Wetin you don father?’ or to woman, ‘Wetin you don bring forth?’”
Di Lord, di Holy One of Israel, and im Maker, talk like dis: “Ask me of things to come concerning my children, and concerning di work of my hands, command me.
I don make di earth, and create man on am. I, even my hands, don stretch out di heavens, and I don command all dem army.
I don raise am up in righteousness, and I go make straight all im ways. E go build my city, and e go let my exiles go free, no for price nor reward,” talk di Lord of Armies.

Di Lord talk like dis: “Di labour of Egypt, and di merchandise of Cush, and di Sabeans, men of stature, go come over to you, and dem go be yours. Dem go follow you. Dem go come over in chains. Dem go bow down to you. Dem go make supplication to you, saying, ‘Surely God dey with you, and dey no other. Dey no other god.’”
Truly you be God wey hide imself, God of Israel, di Saviour.
Dem go dey ashamed, yes, confounded, all of dem. Dem go go in confusion together, wey be makers of idols.
Israel go dey saved by di Lord with everlasting salvation. Una no go dey ashamed nor confounded to ages of eternity.
Because di Lord wey create di heavens, di God wey form di earth and make am, wey establish am and no create am waste, wey form am to dey inhabited, talk like dis: “I be di Lord, and dey no other.
I no speak in secret, for place for di land of darkness. I no talk to di offspring of Jacob, ‘Seek me in vain.’ I, di Lord, speak righteousness. I declare things wey dey right.
Assemble yourselves and come. Draw near together, una wey don escape of di nations. Dem no get knowledge wey carry di wood of dem engraved image, and pray to god wey no fit save.

Declare and present your case. Yes, make dem take counsel together. Who don show dis from ancient time? Who don declare am of old? No be me, di Lord? Dey no other God beside me, righteous God and Saviour. Dey none beside me.
Look to me, and dey saved, all di ends of di earth, because I be God, and dey no other.
I don swear by myself. Di word don go out of my mouth in righteousness, and no go return, say to me every knee go bow, every tongue go swear.
Dem go talk of me, ‘Only for di Lord dey righteousness and strength.’ Men go come to am. All wey dey angry against am go dey ashamed.
For di Lord all di offspring of Israel go dey justified, and go glory.”
Bel don bow down. Nebo stoop. Dem idols dey on di animals and on di livestock. Di things wey una carry dey loaded, burden for di weary animal.
Dem stoop. Dem bow down together. Dem no fit deliver di burden, but dem imself don go into captivity.
“Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all di remnant of di house of Israel, wey I don carry from di womb, wey I don bear from di womb:
even to your old age I be am, and even to grey hairs I go carry you. I don make, and I go bear. Yes, I go carry, and I go deliver.
To who una go liken me, and make me equal, and compare me, so that we go dey like?
Dem wey lavish gold out of di bag, and weigh silver for di balance, dem hire goldsmith, and e make am god. Dem fall down. Yes, dem worship.
Dem bear am on di shoulder. Dem carry am, and set am for im place, and e stand. E no go move from im place. Yes, one go cry to am, yet e no fit answer, nor save am out of im trouble.
Remember dis, and show yourselves men. Bring am again to mind, una transgressors.
Remember di former things of old, because I be God, and dey no other. I be God, and dey none like me,
declaring di end from di beginning, and from ancient times di things wey never dey done, saying, ‘My counsel go stand, and I go do all my pleasure.’
Calling bird of prey from di east, di man of my counsel from far country. Yes, I don speak. I go also bring am to pass. I don purpose. I go also do am.
Listen to me, una stubborn-hearted, wey dey far from righteousness:
I bring my righteousness near. E no go dey far off, and my salvation no go delay. I go place salvation for Zion, for Israel my glory.”
“Come down, and sit for di dust, virgin daughter of Babylon. Sit on di ground without throne, daughter of di Chaldeans, because dem no go call you tender and delicate again.
Take di millstones, and grind meal. Remove your veil, strip off di skirt, uncover di legs, pass through di rivers.
Your nakedness go dey uncovered. Yes, your shame go dey seen. I go take vengeance, and I no go meet you as man.”
Our Redeemer, di Lord of Armies na im name, di Holy One of Israel.
“Sit silent, and go into darkness, daughter of di Chaldeans, because dem no go call you di mistress of kingdoms again.
I dey angry with my people. I don profane my inheritance, and give dem into your hand. You show dem no mercy. On di aged you lay your yoke very heavily.
You talk, ‘I go be mistress forever,’ so that you no lay dis things to heart, neither you remember di end of dem.
Now therefore hear dis, you wey dey given to pleasures, wey dwell securely, wey talk for your heart, ‘I be, and dey none beside me. I no go sit as widow, neither I go know loss of children.’

But two things go come to you for one moment, for one day: loss of children and widowhood. Dem go come on you in full measure, despite di multitude of your sorceries, despite di great power of your enchantments.
You don trust for your wickedness. You don talk, ‘No one dey see me.’ Your wisdom and your knowledge don mislead you. You don talk for your heart, ‘I be, and dey none beside me.’
But evil go come on you. You no go know how to charm am away. Mischief go fall on you. You no go fit put am off. Desolation go come on you suddenly, wey you no know.
Stand now with your enchantments, and with di multitude of your sorceries, wey you don labour for from your youth. Maybe you go fit profit. Maybe you go prevail.
You dey weary with di multitude of your counsels. Make dem stand up now, and save you, di astrologers, di stargazers, wey predict month by month wetin go come on you.
See, dem go be like stubble. Di fire go burn dem. Dem no go deliver demselves from di power of di flame. Dis no be coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before.
Dem go be to you like dat, wey you don labour with, wey don trade with you from your youth. Everyone go wander for im own quarter. Nobody go save you.”

“Hear dis, house of Jacob, wey dem call by di name of Israel, and wey come out of di waters of Judah, wey swear by di name of di Lord, and make mention of di God of Israel, but no in truth, nor in righteousness.
Because dem call demselves of di holy city, and rely on di God of Israel. Di Lord of Armies na im name.
I don declare di former things from of old. Yes, dem go out of my mouth, and I showed dem. Suddenly I do dem, and dem come to pass.
Because I know say you dey obstinate, and your neck na iron sinew, and your forehead brass,
I don declare am to you from of old. Before e come to pass I showed am to you, so that you no go talk, ‘My idol don do dem, and my engraved image, and my molten image, don command dem.’
You don hear. See all dis. And una no go declare am? I don show you new things from dis time, even hidden things, wey you no know.
Dem dey created now, and no from of old. Before today you no hear dem, so that you no go talk, ‘See, I know dem.’
Yes, you no hear. Yes, you no know. Yes, from of old your ear no open, because I know say you deal very treacherously, and dem call you transgressor from di womb.
For my name sake I go defer my anger, and for my praise I go hold am back from you, so that I no go cut you off.
See, I don refine you, but no as silver. I don choose you for di furnace of affliction.
For my own sake, for my own sake, I go do am, because how dem go profane my name? I no go give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and Israel my called: I be he. I be di first. I also be di last.
Yes, my hand don lay di foundation of di earth, and my right hand don spread out di heavens. When I call to dem, dem stand up together.
All of una, assemble yourselves, and hear. Who among dem don declare dis things? Di Lord don love am. E go perform im pleasure for Babylon, and im arm go dey on di Chaldeans.
I, even I, don speak. Yes, I don call am. I don bring am, and e go make im way prosper.
Come near to me, hear dis: from di beginning I no speak in secret. From di time wey e dey, I dey dere. Now di Lord God don send me, and im Spirit.”
Di Lord, your Redeemer, di Holy One of Israel, talk like dis: “I be di Lord your God, wey teach you to profit, wey lead you by di way wey you go go.
Oh say you don listen to my commandments! Den your peace for don be like river, and your righteousness like di waves of di sea.
Your offspring for don be like di sand, and di offspring of your body like di grains of am. Im name no for don dey cut off nor destroyed from before me.”
Go out from Babylon! Flee from di Chaldeans! Declare with voice of singing. Tell dis, utter am to di end of di earth. Talk, “Di Lord don redeem im servant Jacob.”
Dem no thirst when e lead dem through di deserts. E cause di waters to flow out of di rock for dem. E split di rock also, and di waters gush out.
“Dey no peace,” talk di Lord, “for di wicked.”
Listen, islands, to me, and listen, una peoples, from far. Di Lord don call me from di womb. From di body of my mother, e don make mention of my name.
E don make my mouth like sharp sword. For di shadow of im hand e don hide me. E don make me polished arrow. For im quiver e don keep me close.
E talk to me, “You be my servant, Israel, in whom I go dey glorified.”
But I talk, “I don labour in vain. I don spend my strength for nothing and vanity. Yet surely my justice dey with di Lord, and my reward with my God.”
Now di Lord wey form me from di womb to be im servant, to bring Jacob again to am, and make Israel dey gathered to am (for I dey honourable for di eyes of di Lord, and my God don become my strength),

yes, e talk, “Na small thing say you be my servant to raise up di tribes of Jacob, and to restore di preserved of Israel. I go also give you for light to di nations, so that you go be my salvation to di end of di earth.”

Di Lord, di Redeemer of Israel, im Holy One, talk like dis to am wey man despise, to am wey di nation abhor, to di servant of rulers: “Kings go see and rise up. Princes go see and worship, because of di Lord wey dey faithful, even di Holy One of Israel, wey don choose you.”

Di Lord talk like dis: “For acceptable time I don answer you. For day of salvation I don help you. I go preserve you, and give you for covenant of di people, to raise up di land, to make dem inherit di desolate heritages,
to talk to di prisoners, ‘Go out,’ to dem wey dey for darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ Dem go feed by di ways. Dem pastures go dey for all bare heights.
Dem no go hunger nor thirst. Neither di scorching heat nor sun go strike dem, because e wey get mercy on dem go lead dem, even by di springs of water e go guide dem.
I go make all my mountains road, and my highways go dey raised up.
See, dem go come from far. See, dem from di north and from di west, and dem from di land of Sinim.”
Sing, una heavens, and dey joyful, earth! Break out into singing, una mountains! Because di Lord don comfort im people, and go have compassion on im afflicted.
But Zion talk, “Di Lord don forsake me, and di Lord don forget me.”
“Woman fit forget her nursing child, so that she no go have compassion on di son of her womb? Yes, even dem fit forget, yet I no go forget you.
See, I don engrave you on di palms of my hands. Your walls dey continually before me.
Your children dey hurry. Your destroyers and dem wey make you waste go leave you.

Lift up your eyes all round, and see. All dem gather demselves together, and come to you. As I live,” talk di Lord, “you go surely clothe yourself with dem all as with ornament, and bind dem on as bride.
Because for your waste and your desolate places, and your land wey dem don destroy, now you go dey too narrow for di inhabitants, and dem wey swallow you up go dey far away.
Di children of your bereavement go still talk for your ears, ‘Di place too narrow for me. Give place to me so that I fit dwell.’

Den you go talk for your heart, ‘Who don bear me dis, seeing say I don lose my children, and dey solitary, exile, and wandering to and fro? Who don bring up dis? See, I dey left alone. Dem, where dem dey?’”
Di Lord God talk like dis: “See, I go lift up my hand to di nations, and set up my banner to di peoples. Dem go bring your sons for dem arms, and your daughters go dey carried on dem shoulders.

Kings go be your foster fathers, and dem queens your nursing mothers. Dem go bow down to you with dem faces to di earth, and lick up di dust of your feet. Den you go know say I be di Lord, and dem wey wait for me no go dey ashamed.”
Di prey go dey taken from di mighty? Or di lawful captives delivered?

But di Lord talk like dis: “Even di captives of di mighty go dey taken away, and di prey of di terrible go dey delivered, because I go contend with am wey contend with you, and I go save your children.

I go feed dem wey oppress you with dem own flesh, and dem go dey drunk with dem own blood, as with sweet wine. All flesh go know say I, di Lord, na your Saviour, and your Redeemer, di Mighty One of Jacob.”

Di Lord talk like dis: “Where di certificate of your mother divorce, wey I don send her away? Or which of my creditors be di one wey I don sell una to? See, for una iniquities una don sell yourselves, and for una transgressions una mother don dey sent away.

Why, when I come, nobody dey? When I call, nobody answer? My hand dey too short to redeem? Or I no get power to deliver? See, with my rebuke I dry up di sea. I make di rivers wilderness. Dem fish stink because no water dey, and die for thirst.
I clothe di heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth dem covering.”
Di Lord God don give me di tongue of those wey dey taught, so that I go know how to sustain with words am wey dey weary. E wake me morning by morning. E wake my ear to hear as those wey dey taught.
Di Lord God don open my ear, and I no dey rebellious, neither I turn away back.
I give my back to di strikers, and my cheeks to dem wey pluck off di beard. I no hide my face from shame and spitting.
Because di Lord God go help me, therefore I no dey disgraced. Therefore I don set my face like flint, and I know say I no go dey ashamed.
E dey near wey justify me. Who go contend with me? Make we stand up together. Who be my adversary? Make am come near to me.
See, di Lord God go help me. Who be im wey go condemn me? See, dem all go wear out like garment. Di moth go eat dem up.
Who among una fear di Lord, and obey di voice of im servant? Im wey waka for darkness, and no get light, make am trust for di name of di Lord, and rely on im God.

See, all una wey kindle fire, wey surround yourselves with torches, waka for di flame of your fire, and among di torches wey una don kindle. Dis na wetin una go get from my hand: una go lie down for sorrow.
